newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends mostly lower, liquidation in May.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends mostly lower, liquidation in May.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended mostly lower on Wednesday, led by the May on liquidation ahead of first notice day next Wednesday, traders said.
"It was mostly rollover (trade) from the May to the July," a pit source said. "The spread traded from even to three cents, premium May, on the day."
The May/July spread closed at 1/2 cent, premium May.

Farmer hedging continued to weaken new crop prices despite the slow plantings pace. In Texas, the rice crop was 12 percent planted. That figure compares to 69 percent a year ago, and the five-year average of 54 percent.

Results of a Costa Rican rice tender were still up in the air but floor sources said it likely was cancelled. A U.S. rice source said two offers had been withdrawn, adding to ideas the sale would not be completed.
Rice ended five cents per cwt lower to one cent higher with May off three at $11.58.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 750 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 315 lots.
